summary: The recorded base reproduces the issue-specific LoRA accounting failure in the actual checked-out _handle_batch_request implementation and hangs the real LoRARegistry zero wait. At the exact candidate commit, the submitted regression and independent n=16 and mixed-adapter unload-contract tests pass. The candidate narrowly removes tokenizer-side LoRA release ownership from the unacquired prefix warm-up request while preserving scheduler-side adapter identity. No counterexample was found in the directly affected lifecycle, but the exact Qwen3.5 HTTP/model scenario could not be run, so full original deployment resolution remains unverified.

tests.what_was_measured: The candidate regression independently failed on the recorded base: 5 releases for 4 acquisitions and 8 releases for 6 acquisitions; n=1 passed.
All three submitted lifecycle cases passed at exact candidate commit 974cd3283b0360c7f2c71b044edbe3438c3d13b9.
The real LoRARegistry wait_for_unload timed out after the reported three-request n=16 traffic shape and after a mixed adapter-A/no-adapter/adapter-B batch.
The real LoRARegistry reached zero and unloaded after three independent n=16 lifecycles; mixed adapters also unloaded, and scheduler warm-up requests retained the correct adapter IDs.
Candidate Python source and regression compiled successfully.
Candidate diff contains no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: Prepared Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 detected exactly one AMD Instinct MI350X with gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- and executed a tensor sum. This establishes assigned-GPU availability only; no model serving or GPU kernel claim is based on it.

remaining_limitations: The reported Qwen3.5-0.8B model and rank-128 LoRA weights were unavailable, so the full HTTP serving deadlock and recovery were not exercised on the reported hybrid architecture.
The available environment is ROCm 7.2 on gfx950, while both reported reproductions used CUDA 13.1 on NVIDIA architectures.

The deterministic tests execute the actual checked-out request method and real registry/counter but use controlled tokenizer and scheduler-response doubles; they validate lifecycle accounting rather than model semantics.
No native source changed in the candidate, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
